# A Social Club Reclaimed 10-15 Hours a Week Using ChatGPT Work

> **In short:** According to OpenAI, a social club called The Den now finishes grant applications in 2 hours instead of 3 days, and liquor-license paperwork in 3 hours instead of 4 — freeing 10-15 hours a week to focus on opening a new location.

A small business owner just bought back a full day or two every week — not by hiring, but by handing the boring paperwork to an AI assistant. Here's what that looks like in real life, and what the rest of us can take from it.

## The story behind the savings

The Den is a social club, and according to OpenAI's announcement, the team is opening a new location. Expansion usually means a tall stack of government forms, lawyer emails, and weeks of back-and-forth.

Two specific tasks in the case study stand out:

- **Grant applications.** What used to take the team about 3 days now takes about 2 hours, OpenAI says.
- **Liquor-license materials.** What used to take about 4 days now takes about 3 hours.

Add it up, and OpenAI says The Den is getting back roughly 10 to 15 hours every week — hours the team can now spend on the parts of the job that actually grow the business.

## What "ChatGPT Work" is

The Den is using a version of ChatGPT that OpenAI calls **ChatGPT Work** — the work-focused side of the tool, aimed at the writing and research that come up in a working day. In this case, the work was turning what the team already knew about the business into the long, structured documents grant bodies and licensing offices ask for. That's the kind of writing — taking your own facts and reshaping them into a specific format — where AI tends to be most useful. You feed it the information, and it produces a first draft you can review and edit.

## What's worth taking from this

- **Time savings come from drafting, not deciding.** The Den didn't use AI to decide which grants to apply for or whether the new location made sense. It used AI to turn decisions the team had already made into the right format, fast.
- **Paperwork is where most small businesses leak time.** Grants, licenses, leases, vendor contracts — the documents a growing business needs but nobody enjoys writing.
- **The first draft is the real win.** Even if a human still needs to check the final version, getting to a strong first draft in 2 hours instead of 3 days changes how a small team plans its week.

## What this means for you

- **If you run a small business or side project:** Look at the writing tasks on your plate this week — anything where you already have the answers but need to put them in a specific format. Those are usually the best first candidates for an AI assistant.
- **If you're a freelancer or solopreneur:** The same idea applies. Proposals, contracts, applications, client summaries — start with the items that follow a template, and treat AI as your first-draft helper, not your final say.
- **If you're just curious about ChatGPT Work:** It's the work-focused side of ChatGPT, built for documents and company questions rather than casual chat. OpenAI has more details on its own site if you want to see exactly what's included.
- **If you already use it:** Try giving it a past document you've already written — a grant, an application, a contract — and ask it to use the same structure for something new. A faster first draft is usually the goal, not a perfect one.

## Wrap-up

A social club cut days of paperwork down to hours using ChatGPT Work, according to OpenAI. The lesson for the rest of us isn't "AI does everything" — it's that the boring, format-heavy writing in your week is probably where the easiest time savings are hiding. Pick one document you keep putting off, draft it with AI, and see how much of your week you get back.
